summary: Mainstream application frameworks and architecture-testing tools support feature-local organization, although each enforces a different part of the pattern.

items.text: Angular's official style guide says to group closely related files in the same directory, keep tests beside the code they test, organize a project by feature area, and avoid top-level directories named only by artifact type such as components or services. This is an explicit implementation of feature-folder locality.

Next.js App Router treats folders as route segments while allowing project files to be safely colocated inside route folders; private folders and route groups provide non-routable organization boundaries. A feature can therefore own its UI, loading/error states, tests, and helpers without exposing every file as a route.

Nx documents organizing workspace libraries by scope and grouping projects into folders, then uses tags and module-boundary rules to constrain dependencies between those feature or domain units. It supplements physical locality with an enforceable dependency model.

NestJS modules encapsulate related providers and expose only explicitly exported providers. Keeping a module's controllers, services, tests, and configuration together gives a framework-level feature boundary rather than a directory convention alone.
